title: SWF a11y: object 'Make accessible'=false (enabled:false) never emits _accProps.silent — disabled objects stay in screen-reader tree
description:
QA FINDING (manual sweep 2026-06-18, HEAD 27448d0; follow-up to task 1202 feat(a11y), commit 74c0f87).

EXPECTED (Flash 8): Unchecking 'Make object accessible' in the Accessibility panel (ObjectAccessibility.enabled === false) must hide that instance from MSAA screen readers. Flash 8 does this by setting _accProps.silent = true on the instance (AS2: mc._accProps = {silent:true}).

ACTUAL: The _accProps DoAction emit in packages/swf/src/compiler/frames.ts (added by 1202, lines ~961-1006) only emits _accProps for name / description / shortcut / forceSimple. It NEVER consults ObjectAccessibility.enabled. So an instance whose 'Make object accessible' box is unchecked (enabled:false) and which has no name/desc/shortcut/forceSimple/tabIndex emits NOTHING — the object remains exposed to screen readers, contradicting the panel checkbox. The 'enabled' field IS read in the tabOrder path (frames.ts:954 'const tabEnabled = displayObj.accessibility.enabled !== false') but is ignored by the _accProps path.

MODEL: ObjectAccessibility.enabled exists (packages/core/src/engine/types.ts:414, 'Whether this object is included in the accessibility tree. Default: true.'). The accessibility test suite stores enabled:false in the model (packages/swf/src/__tests__/accessibility.test.ts:373) but has NO test asserting the SWF output contains _accProps.silent=true when enabled:false — which is why unit tests are green despite the gap.

REPRO:
  1. Place a movieclip instance with an instanceName.
  2. In the Accessibility panel uncheck 'Make object accessible' (sets accessibility.enabled=false).
  3. Publish. Inspect the DoAction tags — no _accProps.silent is emitted for the instance.
  EXPECTED: a DoAction setting _root.<name>._accProps = {silent:true} (or merging silent:true into the existing _accProps when other fields are also set).

FIX SKETCH: In frames.ts, add 'enabled === false' to the hasX gate (treat as 'has silent'), and emit '_ap.silent = true;' when accessibility.enabled === false. Note: when enabled:false AND other a11y fields are set, Flash still effectively silences the object — preserve that. Add a unit test in accessibility.test.ts asserting _accProps + 'silent' present for enabled:false (mirror the existing forceSimple test at line 612).

This is a fidelity gap automated tests miss; not a crash. Document-level DocumentAccessibility.enabled (EnableAccessibility flag) is a separate concern and out of scope here.
